# How the kickstarter and the console use packages

This page is for administrators and hosting teams who install from the command line, in scripts, CI or containers.
It answers: how you name the site package, where it is fetched from, how that differs from the web wizard, and how
to check the packages before a real run.

## Contents

1. [Same steps, no browser](#same-steps-no-browser)
2. [Naming the site package](#naming-the-site-package)
3. [How the package is found](#how-the-package-is-found)
4. [Differences from the web wizard](#differences-from-the-web-wizard)
5. [Dry runs check the packages](#dry-runs-check-the-packages)
6. [Installing a package that is not on the server](#installing-a-package-that-is-not-on-the-server)
7. [Getting a fresh copy](#getting-a-fresh-copy)

## Same steps, no browser

The kickstarter (`php bin/php/console exp:kickstarter run --apply`, also `php bin/php/kickstarter.php run --apply`) runs the steps of
`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_data.php` from Welcome to Final, each step reading its section of `kickstart.ini` in the
installation root. `exp:install` (`bin/php/install.php`) turns its options into the same sections and runs the same
steps. The package code is therefore the code of the web wizard, described in
[How the setup wizard uses packages](how-the-setup-wizard-uses-packages.md); only the choice of the package and the
fetching rules differ.

## Naming the site package

**kickstart.ini:**

```ini
[site_types]
Continue=true
Site_package=sevenx_multisite
```

`Site_package` is required; its value is the `<name>` of a site package (`kickstart.ini-dist` documents it as "Which
site package to install, package identifier"). `php bin/php/console exp:kickstarter ini --yes` writes
`sevenx_multisite` (`kernel/classes/expkickstarterini.php`).

**exp:install:**

```bash
php bin/php/console exp:install --apply --package=sevenx_multisite
php bin/php/console exp:install --apply --package=cjw_multisite --languages=ger-DE
```

`--package=<name>` defaults to `sevenx_multisite` and becomes `[site_types] Site_package` of the generated
configuration. Without any option, `exp:install` installs `sevenx_multisite` on SQLite.

> **Note**
> The kernel still has a `SitePackages` step (`ezstep_site_packages.php`) that would read a `[site_packages]
> Packages` key, but the step is commented out of `StepTable`, and `kickstart.ini-dist` does not mention it.
> Additional packages cannot be chosen this way; list them as requirements of the site package instead. From 6.0.15
> on their own requirements are downloaded too, down the whole chain. The step stays off: see
> [How the setup wizard uses packages](how-the-setup-wizard-uses-packages.md).

## How the package is found

In kickstart mode `eZStepSiteTypes::init()` does this:

1. Read the remote index (`[RepositorySettings] RemotePackagesIndexURL`, `index.xml`), falling back to
   `var/storage/packages/7x/index.xml` when the server cannot be reached.
2. Read the local site packages and the status of their requirements.
3. Merge the two lists **preferring the remote entry** (`createSitePackagesList( ..., true )`): the index's
   `version` cannot be compared with a local package's version, so the remote entry is kept whenever both exist.
4. Find the entry named by `Site_package`.
5. **The entry has a URL** (it is in the index): call `downloadAndImportPackage()` **without force**. A package of
   that name that is already imported is used as it is; only a missing one is downloaded and imported. Then
   `downloadDependantPackages()` fetches requirements that are missing or older than their `min-version`.
6. **The entry has no URL** (only local, for example in an offline install with a local index that does not list it):
   go on only when every requirement is imported; otherwise the step stops and asks.
7. Select the package and continue with the next step.

The installation itself happens in Create sites, exactly as in the wizard: the required packages are installed in
the order of the site package's `<require>` list.

## Differences from the web wizard

| | Web wizard | Kickstarter and `exp:install` |
|---|---|---|
| Choice | radio button, preselected first imported package | `Site_package` / `--package` |
| Remote and local entry both exist | the newer by version | always the remote entry |
| Remote entry chosen, package already imported | removed and downloaded again (force) | the imported copy is used |
| Requirements | missing or too old: downloaded | the same |
| Upload of an `.ezpkg` | on the page | not offered: import first with `ezpm import` |
| Dry run | none | `--dry-run` |

So with the command line front ends an imported package is never replaced by a run. This is what makes an offline or
pinned install repeatable, and it is also why an old imported package keeps being used after the server has a newer
one; see [Getting a fresh copy](#getting-a-fresh-copy).

## Dry runs check the packages

```bash
php bin/php/console exp:kickstarter run --dry-run
php bin/php/console exp:install --package=sevenx_multisite --dry-run
```

In a dry run `SiteTypes` imports into a temporary repository, `var/storage/packages/dryrun`, and in "skip existing"
mode downloads the site package and **all** its requirements from the server, so the whole chain is verified even
when copies are already imported. The temporary repository is removed when the step is done and at the start of
every run (`expKickstarter::cleanupDryRun()`). A dry run stops after Site details and writes no database and no
settings. Its last line on success:

```text
Dry-run completed: database and remote packages verified. Stopped after SiteDetails, nothing written.
```

Run it before every real install on a server, and after you change `RemotePackagesIndexURL`.

## Installing a package that is not on the server

1. Import the archive into the local repository (from the installation root):

   ```bash
   php ezpm.php import my_site.ezpkg
   php ezpm.php import my_site_classes.ezpkg
   ```

   Import every package it requires too.
2. Name it in `kickstart.ini` or with `--package=my_site`.
3. When the server's index does not list it, the step takes the local copy and goes on as long as every requirement
   is imported (step 6 above).

To let every installation offer such a package, publish it on a package server and point the installations at it:
see [Running your own package server](../your-own/running-your-own-package-server.md) and
[Pointing a site at your package server](../your-own/pointing-a-site-at-your-package-server.md), or contribute it to
the shared server.

## Getting a fresh copy

Because an imported package is reused, remove the imported directory before a run when you want the server's
current archive (the kickstarter documentation says the same: "To force a fresh copy of a package, remove its
imported directory first"). Use the package list's **Remove** in Setup > Packages, or `php ezpm.php delete <name>`;
both delete only the repository copy, not what an install put on a site. See
[Import versus install](import-versus-install.md).
